1) Preconditions
- You must sign in to GitLab with the account that will own the token and that is a member of the fdseChatops group.
- If you use a self‑hosted GitLab instance, substitute your instance base URL (e.g., https://gitlab.example.com) for gitlab.com in the test commands below.

2) Create the Personal Access Token in the web UI
- Sign in to GitLab.
- Click your avatar (top-right) → Preferences (or User Settings) → Access Tokens.
- Give the token a Name, e.g. fdseChatops-token.
- (Optional) Set an expiry date.
- Under Scopes, check api.
- Click Create personal access token.
- Immediately copy the generated token value shown on screen (it will not be shown again).

3) Export the token into your shell (temporary)
- In the shell where you will run GitLab API calls:
  export GITLAB_TOKEN'PASTE_THE_TOKEN_HERE'

4) Persist the token across sessions (optional)
- To persist in bash:
  printf "export GITLAB_TOKEN'%s'\n" "PASTE_THE_TOKEN_HERE" >> ~/.bashrc
  source ~/.bashrc
- Or append the same export to ~/.profile, ~/.zshrc, etc., depending on your shell.

5) Verify the token works
- Test by fetching your user info:
  curl --header "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_TOKEN" "https://gitlab.com/api/v4/user"
- The response should be your user JSON. If it returns 401 Unauthorized, re-check the token, that it has api scope, and that you copied it correctly.

6) Security notes
- Treat the token like a password: do not commit it to git or share it in logs.
- Use the shortest practical expiry and the least privileges necessary.
- If you need an automated token for a project rather than a user, consider a project access token or a deploy token with appropriate scope and permissions.
